text: Each node will make decisions about whether to access the channel or not by itself. So it will follow separate rules, right? But it will make the decision whether to access the channel or not, what to do, based on what it observes in the system. So for example, on the state of the channel. So if that node senses the channel as busy or idle, and it will make the decision by itself. And every node will do that, and every node will follow the same rules. Access point, user nodes, all of them follow the same, more or less always the same rules. Okay, and make decisions by themselves. That's a distributed scheme. The second one that we are going to mention later is instead centralized. What does it mean? It means that the decisions on whether one node should access the channel when are made by only one node in the network. And this node in the network is the access point. So this means that the first scheme can be implemented both when we have the BSS with access point, as well as when we have the BSS in.
